requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill` states no obligation about libraries, algorithms, signatures, types, fields or delegation. It has two kinds of clause.

- **"Habeas MUST bundle a skill".** The deliverable is the skill document. The bundling mechanism is discretionary. Any packaging that ships the document, such as the `Cargo.toml` `package.metadata.symposium.skills` `source.path = "assets/skills"` entry, gives the same observable result. Another packaging mechanism would not violate the clause. `Cargo.toml` already carries its own marker for `requirements.integration.symposium`.
- **The "MUST direct agents to..." clauses.** These cover reading code and tests, mapping every first-party test, mapping every source unit that implements end-user-visible functionality, and reporting gaps without claiming complete coverage absent an independent inventory review. They constrain what the document says, which is observable content. They don't constrain how code is built.

The supplied root, `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`, contains that content, so the content clauses are met there:

- Workflow step 2 directs reading the existing requirements, documentation, entry points, implementation and tests.
- The Inventories section lists every first-party test and every function, method, struct, enum and union, plus the observable surface.
- The Tagging section requires each test to have a `{test}` reference. It also requires each other inventoried item to be mapped to a requirement through a root that reaches it.
- Workflow step 8 calls for a fresh-subagent independent recount.
- The gap list and the Report section make the skill report gaps. They allow claiming 100% only when the recount agrees and no items are unmapped.

No further structural implementation root is needed.

behavioral: The requirement's obligations are all covered by `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories]`.

- **Bundled skill.** The test asserts that `SKILLS` contains `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`. It also asserts that the skill's front-matter description begins "Use when adopting Habeas in an existing codebase". The skill text is read through `skill_files`, which uses `include_str!` on `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`. Because the file must exist at compile time, a missing file fails the build. `bundled_skills_are_five_skill_directories_each_home_to_its_topics` also checks that the `assets/skills` directories match `SKILLS`.
- **Read the code and tests.** `assert_phrases` requires "Read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests" and "Follow behavior through the code".
- **Map every first-party test to a requirement or example.** The test requires "every first-party runnable test or test case", the instruction to record each test's behavior, and "Every test must end up with a `{test}` reference to a requirement or example".
- **Map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality.** The test requires the item inventory phrase "every function, method, struct, enum, and union, listed from the source…". It also requires the phrase on public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors and distinct observable branches. It requires the warning that a tagged entry point doesn't mean every branch beneath it has a requirement, and the instruction "Give every inventoried test and each requirement's roots their references".
- **Report gaps and don't claim completeness without an independent review.** `assert_in_order` requires, in this order, the recount "…without your lists", the gap-report line format, "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items", and "Don't silently exclude difficult cases".

The subject is a document-content requirement. Phrase assertions on the bundled text are the only observable way to test it. The assertions are real: `assert_text` and `assert_text_in_order` panic when a phrase is missing or out of order. I found no clause that goes unasserted.
